info.name: Fluxel — Local Crypto/Fiat API
info.description:
Every HTTP route currently registered in `api/src/routes/*` (v1 public API, health, inbound provider callbacks). 

Before using: set the `sk_key` collection variable — see README.md in this repo (or `local.env.example` + the docker-compose Quickstart) for how to mint one via `xtask bootstrap-test-business`. There is currently no HTTP route to create a business or mint a key — this is deliberate, documented in `xtask/src/bootstrap_test_business.rs`'s own doc comment.

Every error response (any 4xx/5xx from `error_map.rs`) has the shape `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`.

variable.description: Full sk_ bearer key from `xtask bootstrap-test-business` — see README.md
Set after running Customers > Create Customer

request.description: No `TenantCtx`, no auth at all (Doc 1 §6.1 step 3/5) — this is the ALB target-group health check path. Expect `200`.
Same as Liveness but checks downstream dependencies. Expect `200` with body `ok` once Postgres/Mongo/Redis are all reachable.

Doc 5 §2.1. `201 {id, status, wallets:"provisioning"}`. Wallet addresses derive asynchronously (outbox → Redis Streams → `cg_wallets` consumer) — wait a couple seconds before calling List Addresses. `name`/`email`/`metadata` are accepted but currently unused server-side (`#[allow(dead_code)]` on those fields).

Doc 5 §2.1. `[{chain, address}]` — 4 entries once derivation completes (bitcoin, ethereum, bsc, tron — bsc shares ethereum's address by design, Doc 11 §1). If this returns empty, `cg_wallets` hasn't processed the `customer.created` event yet; check `worker` logs.

Doc 5 §2.3, Doc 10 §2. `amount` is minor units (kobo for NGN) — `500000` = ₦5,000.00. `amount_mode` is one of `fixed` (default) | `minimum` | `open`. `201 {id, status, expected_amount, va}` — `va` (virtual account) is `null` initially, provisioned asynchronously by `cg.fiat`; needs real Lenco sandbox credentials in `.env.local` (`LENCO_API_TOKEN`/`LENCO_ACCOUNT_UUID`) to actually provision — that's Rust A's domain, not exercised by the crypto-side local stack alone.
Doc 5 §2.3. `{id, customer_id, status, expected_amount, amount_received, expires_at, va}`. `status` is one of `pending|ready|fulfilled|underpaid|expired|failed`.

Doc 5 §2.4, Doc 10 §4. Runs a REAL Lenco name-enquiry call first (Doc 1 §8.6 step 1) — `account_name` must match what Lenco resolves for `bank_code`/`account_number`, or this returns `422 name_mismatch`. Needs real `LENCO_API_TOKEN` in `.env.local` to do anything but fail with `503 provider_unavailable`. `bank_code`/`account_number` here are placeholders — use List Banks + a real Lenco sandbox test account to get values that actually resolve. `customer_id` is optional (business-initiated payouts omit it).
Doc 5 §2.4. `{id, status, amount, destination}`. `status` is one of `requested|held|approved|executing|completed|failed|rejected|uncertain|reversed`.

Doc 5 §2.4, Doc 1 §8.7. `chain` is one of `bitcoin|ethereum|bsc|tron`. `amount` is minor units (wei for ETH/BSC, sat for BTC, sun for TRON) — the example is 0.001 ETH. `destination_address` is validated for chain-correct format (`crypto::is_valid_address`) and checked against Fluxel's own deposit addresses (returns `422 internal_transfer_unavailable` if it matches one of ours — `POST /v1/transfers` for actual internal reroutes doesn't exist yet). `source:"business"` (treasury-initiated withdrawals) is accepted by the request shape but explicitly rejected — only customer-initiated withdrawals are implemented. Broadcasting a real transaction needs the customer's deposit address to actually hold funds and a real `ALCHEMY_API_KEY`/`TRON_API_KEY` in `.env.local` — with neither, this creates the record (`201`) but `withdrawal_executor` will fail safely on insufficient balance.

Doc 5 §2.4. `{id, status, chain, asset_code, amount, fee, destination_address, txid, network_fee}`. `status` is one of `processing|pending_review|broadcast|confirmed|failed|rerouted_internal`. `txid`/`network_fee` are `null` until broadcast.
Doc 5 §2.6. `{account_name}` on success. Real Lenco call — needs `LENCO_API_TOKEN`, and real sandbox bank/account values to succeed (the example values are placeholders that will 422).
Doc 5 §2.6. `[{code, name}]` — real Lenco call, cached (`banks_cache` in `LencoProvider`). Use this to get real `bank_code` values for the other fiat requests.

Doc 5 §2.7. `201 {id, secret}` — `secret` is shown once, used to HMAC-verify deliveries (Doc 7 §3). If your receiver runs on your host machine (not in the compose network), use `host.docker.internal` instead of `localhost` so the `worker` container's outbound delivery can actually reach it — `localhost` inside a container means the container itself, not your host (the exact bug `dev_msg/2026-08-06-smoke-test-infra.md` documents hitting during the original sandbox smoke test). Only `customer.wallets.ready` actually fires today — Doc 7 §4's retry schedule/auto-disable/replay aren't built (`worker/src/jobs/webhook_dispatcher.rs` is still a stub).
Confirms the v1 router + auth/tenant middleware pipeline is reachable. `200 {status:"scaffold", doc:"Doc 5 — REST API Specification v1"}`.
Dashboard API is entirely unbuilt (Doc 16 P3) — this is the only route that exists under `/dashboard` right now.

Admin console API is entirely unbuilt (Doc 16 P3) — this is the only route that exists under `/admin` right now. Notably: there is no admin route for business creation or KYB approval either — that's why `xtask bootstrap-test-business` exists (see collection description).

item.name: Lenco Callback (will 401 without a real signature)

request.description: This is Lenco calling FLUXEL, not something a business/customer ever calls directly — included for reference/manual signature-verification testing only. `receive()` verifies the signature against `LencoProvider::verify_webhook` before persisting anything; without a real, correctly-signed payload this always returns `401`. Any `:provider` value other than `lenco` returns `200` and is ignored (logged, not an error).
